text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- The Prime Minister's office issues plan to privatise 13 companies this year
- Syria releases thousands of reserve soldiers mobilised during tension with Israel
- U.S. rabbi says Netanyahu used services of reform rabbi in his second marriage. PM office denies.
- City of Tel Aviv refuses to release harsh data on air pollution.
JERUSALEM POST
- Bill allowing Israelis abroad to vote passes first reading
- Heavy rain causes chaos
- Government unveils partial privatisation list
- PM: upcoming meeting with Clinton will deal with restarting Syrian talks
- France calls on owners of Nazi-looted art to claim it
- Government releasing more homes in territories for sale
MAARIV
- Storm in knesset over bill to vote abroad
- Arafat: we'll declare a state next year
- Channel One TV: the appointment of Ronnie Bar-On as attorney general was part of deal with Deri giving him a plea bargain in exchange for support for the Hebron deal
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Demands to investigate Deri involvement in Bar-On appointment
- Mordechai Vanunu writes in his handwriting: this is how I was abducted - to be published in Yedioth on Friday
- 15 right-wing legislators demand release of Jewish political killers if Arab killers are released.
GLOBES
- Industrial production grew in 1996 by only 5.5 percent, down from 8.5 percent in 1995. Sharp drop of 3.4 percent in October-November 1996
- Globes reveals: German concern Dagossa melted for the SS gold stolen from Jews
- Generali promised to examine life insurance claims for heirs of Jews killed in Holocaust
- Egyptian Cato group: we'll buy "sizable holding" in Koor concern.
- Moroccan airline to operate in Israel with El-Al
